current_episode.title: How Rugby Tots Builds Confidence Through Play | Tom Brown | Tod Talks

guest.bio_context: Tom Brown is a Rugby Tots franchisee operating in the South Bucks and East Orsa areas. He runs structured play rugby sessions for young children, managing his own team of coaches sourced from local universities and schools. He is also a father himself, which informs his understanding of what young families need from early-years activity programmes.

context.real_quote: We want to build confidence in young children, we want to give opportunity for those lightbulb moments, we want to work on movement literacy to really develop a really supportive platform that children can grow in without really knowing what they're developing.
key_stats: Two-week structured plan: Rugby Tots runs sessions on a two-week cycle so children see an activity one week and can excel at it the next
Two-week money-back guarantee offered to all new Rugby Tots enrolments before full commitment is required
10% refer-a-friend discount offered per referral by Tom Brown's South Bucks and East Orsa franchises, stackable across multiple referrals
50% potential term fee reduction: Tom Brown's example of stacking multiple refer-a-friend discounts over time
Free taster classes available to new families via www.rugbytots.co.uk postcode search

pending_qa.q: How does Rugby Tots use imaginative play to develop physical skills in young children?
pending_qa.r: Rugby Tots uses imaginative framing to teach movement skills without children realising they are learning. For example, asking children to 'stomp like a dinosaur' over hurdles teaches knee-lifting and body movement, while catching and passing is framed as a frog jumping onto a lily pad rather than a throwing drill. This approach taps into children's imagination to make skill development feel like pure play.

pending_qa.q: What is the role of parents and caregivers in Rugby Tots classes?
pending_qa.r: Rugby Tots actively encourages grown-ups to participate in sessions alongside their children. The programme aims to give parents the opportunity to witness their child's lightbulb moments — breakthroughs that children often have at nursery or school but rarely at home with a trusted adult present. As children grow more confident, the programme progressively encourages independence, while always allowing the child to reach back to their grown-up.

pending_qa.q: What trial or money-back options does Rugby Tots offer new families?
pending_qa.r: Rugby Tots offers free taster classes to new families, which can be found by entering a postcode on www.rugbytots.co.uk to locate local classes and franchisee contact details. Beyond the taster, new enrolments receive a two-week money-back guarantee, allowing families to attend more than one session before fully committing.

pending_qa.q: Does Rugby Tots offer any referral discounts for existing members?
pending_qa.r: Tom Brown offers a 10% refer-a-friend discount for the franchises he runs in the South Bucks and East Orsa areas. This discount can be stacked, meaning a family who refers multiple new members could theoretically reduce their term fees significantly — Tom gives the example of potentially paying only 50% per term through ongoing referrals.

pending_qa.q: What type of coaches does Rugby Tots recruit and what is their background?
pending_qa.r: In the South Bucks area, Rugby Tots coaches include students at Brunel University who aspire to become professional rugby players and want to give back to younger generations. Coaches also come from local schools and colleges, and some were Rugby Tots participants themselves who have now moved into coaching roles, creating what Tom describes as full-circle moments.

pending_qa.q: Is Rugby Tots only for children who want to play rugby competitively?
pending_qa.r: No — Rugby Tots is explicitly not a programme requiring children to become rugby players. Tom describes it in its rawest form as a PE class with rugby as the vehicle to deliver movement literacy, confidence-building, and developmental skills. The goal is to create a supportive platform where children grow without necessarily knowing what they are developing.
